name: GFL Environmental
description: GFL collects, hauls, transfers, recycles and buries solid waste in Canada and 18 US states; it calls itself the fourth largest diversified environmental services company in North America. Municipalities and businesses pay it for curbside and container collection under contracts of three to ten years (municipal) or three to five years (commercial), and haulers pay tipping fees to use its transfer stations and landfills. About two thirds of revenue ($4.45 billion of $6.62 billion in 2025) is from the US and one third from Canada. In March 2025 it sold its separate environmental services (hazardous and liquid waste) business for an enterprise value of $8.0 billion and kept about 34 percent of it; long-term debt fell from $10.0 billion to $7.4 billion during 2025 through repayments. It grows mostly by buying local haulers (over 290 acquisitions since 2007) and by price increases.

hq.note: Executive headquarters 1759 Purdy Avenue, Miami Beach, Florida; registered office in Vaughan, Ontario (FY2025 Annual Information Form, 40-F Exhibit 99.1)

employees.note: "approximately 15,000 employees", 44.1% in Canada and 55.9% in the United States; 10% unionized (FY2025 AIF)

businessLines.name: Solid Waste USA
businessLines.how: Households and municipalities pay per household, per service or per lift under multi-year collection contracts; businesses pay monthly for container pickup; haulers pay tipping fees by weight at its transfer stations and landfills. Price increases tied to CPI or waste indices and acquisitions drive growth.
businessLines.description: Collection, transfer, landfill and material recovery operations in 18 US states.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-IFRS), the measure the chief operating decision maker uses; IFRS operating income by segment was not read. Margin 35.0%, up 70 basis points. About 69.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA before Corporate costs of $(262.0)M.

businessLines.name: Solid Waste Canada
businessLines.how: Same model as the US segment: municipal contracts of three to ten years (often directing waste to a municipal or designated facility), commercial contracts of three to five years with CPI and fuel adjustments, plus tipping fees; in some provinces it is also paid by producer responsibility organizations to collect recyclables.
businessLines.description: Collection, transfer, landfill, material recovery and organics operations across Canada.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-IFRS). Margin 31.9%, up 210 basis points. About 30.7% of segment Adjusted EBITDA before Corporate costs.

brands.name: GFL ("Green For Life")
brands.share: Single brand over 100% of continuing revenue; acquired local trade names are not itemized

brands.name: GFL Environmental Services (sold March 2025; now operated by Apollo Funds, BC Funds and HPS)
brands.segment: Hazardous and liquid waste, no longer consolidated
brands.share: GFL holds about 34.0% of the equity (after HPS subscribed for about 22% in September 2025) and has an option to repurchase the balance within five years of the March 2025 closing

brands.name: Green Infrastructure Partners (GIP)
brands.segment: Former Infrastructure Services division, sold April 2022
brands.share: Non-controlling interest retained; GIP recapitalized at a $4.25B enterprise value in September 2025. GFL's percentage was not read.

whatsNext.text: Acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure: SECURE shareholders approved it in May 2026, it is in regulatory review, and GFL targets closing in the latter part of 2026 with an updated outlook to follow
